east_texas.headline: Sunny and cool today. A Freeze Watch is in effect tonight, with Thanksgiving morning near 32 in town and upper 20s in rural low spots.
east_texas.summary: Last night's light showers stayed mostly east of the area, and skies cleared at sunrise. Northwest winds keep highs in the low to mid 50s today and Thanksgiving despite full sunshine. NWS Shreveport has a Freeze Watch for Smith County and most of the region from this evening until 9 AM Thursday, with lows near 32 in town and mid to upper 20s in rural cold spots. Friday morning is close to freezing again before a warming trend brings highs in the 60s Friday and near 70 Saturday.
east_texas.rain_note: No rain expected today through Saturday. A slight chance of a shower north and east of the area Saturday night into Sunday. No improvement to the drought.

panels.title: Why rural low spots freeze first
paras: On clear, calm nights the ground loses heat straight to space, and the air touching it cools fastest. That cold air is heavier, so it slides downhill and pools in creek bottoms, river valleys and open sandy fields. Those spots can run 5 to 8 degrees colder than town, where buildings and pavement hold heat.

That is why NWS Shreveport has about 32 for Tyler tonight while rural low spots fall into the mid to upper 20s. A Freeze Watch runs until 9 AM Thursday, and Friday morning looks similar. Cover tender plants, bring pets in, and protect exposed outdoor faucets.

panels.title: Warm and dry into early December
paras: The Climate Prediction Center strongly favors above-normal temperatures for Texas from Nov 30 to Dec 8, with near to below normal rain for much of the state. Highs in the upper 60s to 70s look likely next week.

Some European ensemble members show a better rain chance around Dec 6 to 8, but that is still far out and confidence is low. El Niño remains very strong, which tends to favor a wetter pattern later in the winter.

tables.title: How cold each morning gets
tables.note: In town means Tyler and other built-up areas. Low spots means rural valleys, creek and river bottoms and sandy open fields, which can run 5 to 8 degrees colder on calm, clear nights. Cover tender plants and bring pets in tonight and Thursday night.

chips.text: Very cold nights in the high valleys
Windy Saturday, gusts 40–50 mph in the highlands

nm.headline: Tranquil late-fall weather through Thanksgiving. Ski areas are opening, and winds pick up Friday and Saturday.
nm.summary: A ridge of high pressure keeps skies mostly sunny and winds light today and Thanksgiving, with temperatures near normal and some high cirrus. Nights stay very cold in the high valleys, with Angel Fire near 12 and Red River near 19 tonight. NWS Albuquerque expects breezy to windy conditions over the highlands Friday afternoon and stronger winds Saturday, with gusts possibly reaching 40 to 50 mph near the central mountain chain. Little or no precipitation is expected.

nm.snow_note: Start-of-day readings for Wednesday. Little change since Tuesday as the snowpack settles in dry weather. Gallegos Peak has doubled its depth over the past week.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu reports 7 inches of new snow over the past 3 days and 15 inches for the season. Red River is projected to open today, and Taos and Ski Santa Fe on Thanksgiving. Resort base depths include man-made snow. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Calm, clear and very cold in the valleys
paras: With light winds and mostly clear skies, cold air pools in the high valleys tonight and Thanksgiving night. NWS has Angel Fire near 12 tonight and 15 Thursday night, Red River near 19, and Taos near 21.
Mountain basins and canyon floors can run colder than forecast on nights like these.

panels.title: Icy stretch on US-64 east of Taos
paras: NMRoads lists US-64 east of Taos (mile markers 257 to 272) and NM-475 to Ski Santa Fe as snow packed and icy. I-40 around Santa Rosa was listed with wet and icy spots on Tuesday.
No closures are listed on the interstates or on NM-518, NM-434, NM-38, NM-75, NM-150 or NM-68.

panels.title: Windy weekend, mild early December
paras: NWS Albuquerque expects windy days Saturday and again Monday with mostly dry shortwaves passing through. Temperatures stay near to above normal.
The Climate Prediction Center favors above-normal temperatures Nov 30 to Dec 8. El Niño is very strong, which tends to favor better snow odds in northern New Mexico as the winter goes on.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, OnTheSnow, Sipapu snow report, NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
